_note: Benefit bullets per instructor (owner request, Oct 1 2026). Fascination-style 'Discover … so you can …'. Numbers appear only where sourced (Ten Commandments: 10 principles; Evolutions: 3 levels, 4 stages; Resonator: 3 documented core themes). Payoffs describe what the buyer can study or practice, never guaranteed dating outcomes. Instructors are referred to by name, not pronouns.

instructors.name: Tyler (Owen Cook)
instructors.headline: Before the bootcamps, Tyler said you should know this first.
bullets: Discover the practical starting point the RSD catalog began with in Foundations, so you can study the mechanics of meeting people and starting conversations before anything advanced.
Uncover the connected framework laid out across the multi-day Blueprint Decoded presentation, so you can understand the thinking behind the techniques instead of memorizing lines.
Watch recorded interactions in Hot Seat at Home with the pause button in your hand, so you can study what was said, how it was delivered, and how the other person responded.
Learn why Tyler wrote in 2007 that his later bootcamps assumed you already knew Foundations, so you can arrive at any live training with the basics already covered.
Compare Tyler's practical "outer game" emphasis with the inner-game programs elsewhere in the archive, so you can decide which approach fits the way you learn.

instructors.name: Madison
instructors.headline: Develop charisma instead of waiting to be born with it.
bullets: Discover how Madison approached conversation, presence, and body language in The Boss, so you can become someone people actually want to talk to.
Learn to break the vague idea of "being charismatic" into parts you can observe and practice: conversation, presence, expression, body language, and voice.
Explore how Madison brought personality into an interaction instead of hiding behind memorized lines, so you can show more of who you are, not less.
Study the role of presentation, energy, and first impressions, so you can become more conscious of how you come across before you say a word.
Connect Madison's inner game with outward behavior, so you can close the gap between how you feel and how you show up in the room.

instructors.name: Julien Blanc
instructors.headline: You've seen Julien's transformation. Now see what came first.
bullets: Discover the earlier dating-focused chapter in PIMP that came before the transformation era, so you can see where the ideas you already know began.
Explore how SHIFT connects beliefs, identity, validation, and motivation to what you actually do in social situations, so you can spot the gap between your self-image and your actions.
Work through TenGame's principle-and-practice approach to offering value, clear communication, and authenticity, so you can turn ideas into something you reflect on and practice.
Compare the earlier chapters with Julien's later personal-transformation work, so you can see the earlier ideas side by side with the ones you already know.
Trace the evolution from outward social performance toward identity and inner work, so you can decide for yourself what changed, what stayed, and what applies to your life.

instructors.name: Jeffy (Jeffrey Allen)
instructors.headline: Same words. Different voice. Different conversation.
bullets: Discover how one of early RSD's most distinctive personalities made personality itself part of the lesson in The Jeffy Show, so you can stop trying to sound like everyone else.
Explore the three documented pillars of The Resonator (vocal projection, storytelling, and humor), so you can work on how you sound, not just what you say.
Find out why delivery can matter as much as content, so you can bring more energy and expression to everyday conversations.
See how Execute the Program 2.0 approached profiles, photos, and messaging, so you can rethink the first impression your online presence makes before you ever speak.
Study the move from digital contact to an actual date, so you can adapt the principles to today's apps instead of copying outdated platform instructions.

instructors.name: Tim
instructors.headline: What if the goal was never to sound like a technique?
bullets: Discover the natural-style branch of RSD in Flawless Natural, so you can study an alternative to heavily structured technique.
Explore the difference between understanding a framework and sounding rehearsed, so you can communicate in a way that still feels like you.
See how attitude and self-expression were treated as part of social skill, so you can pay attention to more than the words you choose.
Compare Tim's approach with the archive's more systematic programs, so you can find where you sit between structure and spontaneity.
Add an instructor perspective from outside the best-known programs, so you can broaden your reference points beyond a single teacher.

instructors.name: Alex Social
instructors.headline: The nightlife and the inner game, taught by the same instructor.
bullets: Discover how Social Encrypted (2015) taught social learning inside the nighttime environment, with instruction and demonstrations, so you can study a setting that intimidates many people.
Explore the inner-game message of No Reason You're Not Enough (2016), so you can examine the internal side of social confidence.
See the outer environment and the inner game covered by one instructor, so you can connect what happens in your head with what happens in the room.
Compare Alex's nightlife material with the archive's daytime, social-circle, and online programs, so you can choose the environment that fits your life.
Study nighttime social dynamics through today's standards of mutual interest and respect for boundaries, so you can keep what's useful and leave outdated assumptions behind.

instructors.name: Brad Branson
instructors.headline: Find your stage. Then look past the single conversation.
bullets: Discover the beginner, intermediate, and advanced perspectives Evolutions is organized around, so you can find the level that matches where you are right now.
Follow Evolutions' four-stage sequence of mindset, approach, conversation, and closing, so you can pinpoint which part of an interaction your questions belong to.
Explore Lifestyle Academy's wider lens on values, career, finances, health, and personal direction, so you can see social confidence as part of a bigger life plan.
Learn how one instructor connected dating with the rest of life, so you can set goals that reach beyond a single conversation.
Study a structured progression instead of a pile of tips, so you can keep the material organized as you work through it.

instructors.name: Derek
instructors.headline: Ten principles. Everything else is tactics.
bullets: Discover the ten principles Ten Commandments of Game is built around, so you can see the foundation beneath individual tactics.
Learn why Derek put principles ahead of lines and routines, so you can respond to the situation in front of you instead of reciting a script.
Use the principle-first structure as a lens for reflection, so you can review your own interactions more clearly.
Compare Derek's ten principles with TenGame's principle-based approach, so you can see where two instructors agree and where they differ.
Study a clear conceptual structure, so you can understand the "why" before worrying about the "what to say".

instructors.name: Luke
instructors.headline: Stop starting from zero every night. Study the social circle.
bullets: Discover how Social Circle Blueprint shifts attention from isolated encounters to social circles, so you can stop starting from zero every time you go out.
Explore how venues, networks, and repeat connections shape a social life, so you can think about the environment around you, not only the next conversation.
Learn the RSD approach to relationships that build over time, so you can work toward a social life people want to be part of.
See how social-circle thinking complements one-to-one confidence, so you can combine both instead of relying on one.
Compare Luke's group-oriented approach with the archive's one-to-one and online material, so you can choose the strategy that fits your lifestyle.

instructors.name: Glenn Ackerman
instructors.headline: A different lens on the emotions behind every interaction.
bullets: Discover Glenn Ackerman's high- and low-vibration framework, so you can examine your emotional patterns through a distinct lens.
Explore how awareness of thoughts and emotions was linked to social interaction, so you can notice your internal state before and during a conversation.
Learn Glenn's language for personal patterns, so you can compare it with how other RSD instructors explained the inner game.
Work through the reflective exercises included in your edition, so you can turn the framework into your own observations.
Study a personal-development perspective presented as the instructor's framework, not medical science, so you can take what's useful and leave the rest.

instructors.name: Multiple RSD instructors + special guests Ozzie & Hoobie
instructors.headline: One problem. Multiple instructors. Completely different answers.
bullets: Discover how several early RSD instructors answered the same social questions in Transformations, so you can compare completely different approaches in one program.
Learn from special guest instructors Ozzie and Hoobie, whose contributions to Transformations add perspectives you won't find in any single instructor's program.
Explore practical technique and inner-game perspectives side by side, so you can see how the two were connected early on.
Notice the differences in teaching style, from the core RSD instructors to the special guests, so you can find the explanations that click for you.
Study the original multi-instructor Transformations, so you can trace where the recorded archive began.

instructors.name: More from the RSD archive
instructors.headline: Two more ways to think about your social world: circles and influence.
bullets: Discover Social Circle Hacking's 24 lessons on social circles, so you can think beyond one conversation at a time.
Compare Social Circle Hacking with Luke's 110-lesson Social Circle Blueprint, so you can see two takes on building a social life.
Explore the 27-lesson Influence Mastery Program, so you can study influence as a skill rather than a personality trait.
Connect influence with the charisma and delivery material from Madison and Jeffy, so you can see how the pieces fit together.
Use your Success Coaching Call to decide where these programs fit in your plan, so you spend your time on what matters to you.
